rules.title: The server is a development server or a proxied production origin, and nothing a proxy does earlier is in it
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no php-fpm and no FastCGI: the origin speaks HTTP/1.1 over TCP or a Unix socket, terminates no TLS and compresses nothing, so nginx's `fastcgi_pass` becomes `proxy_pass`

rules.title: The `[server]` block is `Boot`-class, `listen` is one flat array defaulting to `127.0.0.1:8000` in both modes, and the flag is the last word
rules.divergesFromPhp: `listen` is the origin's own address rather than a php-fpm pool's, and `workers` counts accept cores rather than sizing a `pm.*` process pool

rules.title: A mount matches on `prefix` or `host`, names one `entry` or one `scan`, and a scan expands against the disk at boot
rules.divergesFromPhp: a vhost's rewrite rules become one `[[server.mount]]` block, and a module is relocatable because the matched prefix is stripped before the route table sees the path

rules.title: A mount's key set is `prefix`, `host`, `scan`, `entry` and `origin`; `mode`, limits and capabilities belong to the `[[app]]` block
A `listen` entry beginning with a separator is a Unix socket, Unix-only, with `socket_mode`, and it is the transport a proxy should prefer
rules.divergesFromPhp: the same `listen = /run/nvs.sock` shape as php-fpm, but a Windows host has no named-pipe equivalent and listens on TCP loopback

rules.title: `[mode] ceiling` is `System`-class, bounds a runtime flip and not the startup value, and unset equals the mode the server started in
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `php.ini-development` to copy: a production host that wrote nothing is unreachable from code, and one root-owned line opens it

rules.title: A development-mode server binding a non-loopback address prints a banner, writes one `Warn` record naming the address, and serves
rules.divergesFromPhp: `php -S 0.0.0.0:8000` says nothing; here the bind is announced on the console and in the log stream, and it is not refused

rules.title: A default that is unsafe inbound or unbounded outbound is a defect, not a neutral starting point
rules.divergesFromPhp: php-fpm behind nginx ships no security headers, no cookie flags and no outbound timeout until somebody writes them; here nothing written is already the safe and finite configuration

rules.title: Every `[server] listen` entry is bound before any core accepts, each core holds its own handle on every listener, and `[server] workers` bounds the count over the machine's available parallelism
rules.divergesFromPhp: php-fpm sizes a pool of request *processes* with `pm.*`; `workers` counts accept cores, and one core answers many requests at once

rules.title: `max_in_flight` is a process-wide valve that answers a fixed `503` with `Retry-After` before an isolate exists
rules.divergesFromPhp: php-fpm's `pm.max_children` queues on the socket and the proxy reports a 504; here the origin answers `503` with `Retry-After: 1` itself, and no custom error page runs

rules.title: The effective in-flight ceiling is the smaller of `max_in_flight` and what the memory budget affords, and a clamp is logged once at boot
rules.divergesFromPhp: `pm.max_children` is a free number and the out-of-memory killer enforces its product with memory; here the ceiling is derived from the budget, the configured number is clamped rather than trusted, and the overflow is a `503`

rules.title: Four waits bound a connection, all finite with nothing configured and all idle rather than total
rules.divergesFromPhp: `max_execution_time` and `request_terminate_timeout` bound a whole request; these bound a stalled socket only, so a slow 2 GB upload completes while a stalled one is closed

rules.title: An `accept` that fails on descriptor exhaustion is retried under a bounded backoff and logged once per window
A request resolves by longest mount match, prefix strip, static file, path dispatch, then the entry — and production runs only match, strip, entry
rules.divergesFromPhp: `try_files $uri /index.php` is the development sequence only; in production a URL naming an existing `.nvs` file still runs the mount's entry

rules.title: `trusted_proxies` defaults to empty, empty means the forwarded headers are never read, and a trusted walk takes the rightmost untrusted `X-Forwarded-For` entry
rules.divergesFromPhp: `$_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR']` and `HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR` are replaced by one `clientIp(): ?tainted string`, which is the socket peer until an operator names the proxies

rules.title: `X-Forwarded-For` is the only client-address header read; a trusted peer sending another is warned about, and an untrusted header is ignored, never refused
rules.divergesFromPhp: `X-Real-IP`, `CF-Connecting-IP`, `True-Client-IP`, `Fastly-Client-IP`, `X-Client-IP` and RFC 7239 `Forwarded` are never read, so the common `proxy_set_header X-Real-IP` recipe alone leaves every client as the proxy

rules.title: A forwarded token's port is removed, a withheld address answers `null`, and a token that neither names nor withholds one is a `400`
rules.divergesFromPhp: `clientIp()` is nullable and `null` is an answer, never repaired to `""` or `0.0.0.0`

rules.title: A trusted `X-Forwarded-Proto` sets the effective scheme and HSTS emission and feeds nothing else; no `X-Forwarded-Host` is read
rules.divergesFromPhp: `$_SERVER['HTTPS']` is `Core\Request::scheme()`, set only by a trusted proxy, and a redirect never reconstructs a scheme from it

rules.title: An absent `Host` is a `400`; matching strips the port, folds ASCII case and one trailing dot, refuses non-ASCII, and an unknown host on a host-mounted deployment is a `404`
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `ALLOWED_HOSTS`-style allowlist and no `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']`: the host mounts are the allowlist, and nginx must send `proxy_set_header Host $host`

rules.title: A filesystem path is never derived from a URL at request time
rules.divergesFromPhp: `cgi.fix_pathinfo`, `SCRIPT_FILENAME` and `PATH_INFO` have no counterpart: a request selects a mount from a table expanded at boot and can never name a file

rules.title: A trailing slash is never normalised: `/users` and `/users/` are two URIs
rules.divergesFromPhp: no `DirectorySlash`, no framework redirect and no `rtrim($uri, '/')`: whether the two name one resource is the application's knowledge

rules.title: `HEAD` runs as `GET` with the body discarded and `Content-Length` kept; `method()` reports `Get` and `isHead()` tells the truth
rules.divergesFromPhp: `$_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD']` would say `HEAD`; `Core\Request::method()` says `Get` so the route matches, and `isHead()` is the only place the difference shows

rules.title: A CORS preflight is answered from `[http.cors]` before the unit is loaded, and a plain `OPTIONS` is passed through
rules.divergesFromPhp: no `header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: …')` in application code answers a preflight; the policy answers it before the program exists

rules.title: `[limits] request_body` bounds bytes parsed into memory and `upload_total` bounds a streamed multipart body, each with a hard ceiling, and a route that never reads a body allocates nothing
rules.divergesFromPhp: `upload_max_filesize`, `post_max_size` and `$_FILES['tmp_name']` have no counterpart: there is no temp file, `Core\Request::files()` yields streams, and a route raises its own cap before reading

rules.title: A buffering body reader keeps what it read so another may follow it, and a streaming one consumes the body and is the only reader of it
rules.divergesFromPhp: `$_POST` is populated before the program runs and leaves `php://input` empty for a multipart body; here nothing is read until a member asks, and which reader may follow which is stated rather than decided by `enable_post_data_reading`

rules.title: Static serving is one policy in both modes: the exact file, never a listing, one `ETag`, one `Range`, and a `.nvs` file is never served as source
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `Last-Modified`, no directory index, no `.htaccess` and no `max-age`; `php -S` serving any file under the root, source included, has no counterpart

rules.title: `health_path` is off by default; set, it answers `200` while accepting and `503` while draining, and checks no dependency
rules.divergesFromPhp: php-fpm's `ping.path` and `pm.status_path` have a counterpart that reports no status page, no version and no pool statistics

rules.title: The trace id exists on every request regardless of sampling, is the only request identifier, is emitted on the response, and an inbound `X-Request-ID` is ignored
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `X-Request-ID` and no `$_SERVER['UNIQUE_ID']`; the W3C trace id is the one identifier on every log line, error page and response

rules.title: `[log] access` is a mode default — on in development, off in production — and a `5xx` is logged whatever it says
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no Common or Combined Log Format and no pool `access.log`: the line is a diagnostic record, text in development and JSON in production

rules.title: A deployment that wrote no `[http.headers]` already sends `nosniff`, `frame-ancestors 'none'` and a referrer policy on every response
rules.divergesFromPhp: a php-fpm response carries none of these unless the nginx server block or the application adds them; here they are on every response with nothing configured, and there is no default `Content-Security-Policy` beyond `frame-ancestors`

rules.title: HSTS is emitted when the effective scheme is `https` and not otherwise, and `hsts_subdomains` defaults to `false`
CORS is closed until `[http.cors] origins` names one: no header is emitted and a preflight is answered `403`
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP has no CORS default at all, so a preflight nobody handled is whatever the route does; here it is a `403` until an origin is written

rules.title: `origins = ["*"]` with `credentials = true` is refused at boot and at runtime alike, and so is `same_site = "None"` without `secure`
rules.divergesFromPhp: `header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *')` beside `Allow-Credentials: true` is accepted by PHP and silently rejected by every browser; here the pair does not boot and `Core\Config::set` will not form it

rules.title: Every cookie `Core\Response::addCookie` writes is `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/` unless the call site says otherwise
rules.divergesFromPhp: `setcookie` defaults to no `Secure`, no `HttpOnly` and no `SameSite`; here every cookie starts with all three, `SameSite` is an enum rather than a string, and a script-readable cookie is one written field at the call

rules.title: Every `[http.headers]`, `[http.cors]` and `[http.cookies]` directive is `Runtime` class, and `Core\Response::setHeader` overrides a policy-owned header on one response without logging
A session is a record its store issued: a backend answers `issue`, `load`, `save` and `destroy`, and `load` answering absent is the whole of the strict-id rule
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `SessionHandlerInterface` and no `validateId`; an id the store never issued, one that expired and one an attacker minted are all the same absent answer, and `start` issues a fresh record for each

rules.title: `[session] backend` admits `shared` and `db`, and writing `local` is a boot refusal naming the file it was written in
rules.divergesFromPhp: `session.save_handler = files` and an APCu-backed handler have no counterpart; the choices are the shared tier or the database, and `local` is `E0626` where it is written rather than a session that forgets people

rules.title: A tree with no `[session]` block has no session store, and `start` throws naming the block to write
rules.divergesFromPhp: `session_start()` with nothing configured writes files under `session.save_path`; here a store nobody chose is no store, and the first `start` says which block would choose one

rules.title: A session record is loaded once at `start`, written back whole only when it changed, and never locked
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP holds an exclusive lock on the session for the length of the request, so two requests from one browser serialize; here there is no lock, and two concurrent writes to one session are last-write-wins over the whole record

rules.title: `[session] ttl` is written onto the record and the store expires it; there is no sweeper and no probability of one
rules.divergesFromPhp: `session.gc_probability` and `session.gc_divisor` have no counterpart, because both backends can expire an entry themselves and a filesystem cannot

rules.title: A user's own secret lives in their session, sealed under a key ring through `setSecret` and `getSecret`
rules.divergesFromPhp: `$_SESSION` holds whatever it is given in the clear, and a token in it is readable by anything that can read the store

rules.title: `Core\Request::files()` yields uploaded parts lazily, one at a time, and is the only way to receive one
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `$_FILES` array and no buffered accessor beside the iterator; every application that accepts a file writes a `foreach`, and a part's bytes are readable once, in order

rules.title: A part is a file part iff its `Content-Disposition` carries `filename`; every other part is buffered into `post()`
rules.divergesFromPhp: a part answers `name()`, `filename()` and `contentType()` as tainted strings through members, and there is no `size`, no `tmp_name` and no `error` slot

rules.title: A part is consumed by `readAll`, by walking `content()`, or by `saveTo`, and each way is bounded
rules.divergesFromPhp: `move_uploaded_file` is `saveTo`, `file_get_contents($tmp)` is `readAll` under `request_body`, and a second pass over an upload has to say where the first one put it

rules.title: `request_body` caps bytes parsed into memory and `upload_total` caps a streamed multipart body, and both are `[limits]` rows
rules.divergesFromPhp: `upload_max_filesize` and `post_max_size` are replaced by a cap on what is parsed into memory and a cap on what is streamed past it, and a file's size is never checked against the first

rules.title: `upload_total` is enforced by the server on the wire: a declared oversize is refused before dispatch and a chunked one is stopped at the part being read
There is no temp file: a part lands on disk only where the application names a path under `fs.write`, and disk is the resource it must bound
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no `tmp_name`, no `upload_tmp_dir`, no `move_uploaded_file` and no `is_uploaded_file`; an upload nobody saves is never on disk, and one that is saved is there because the program wrote it

rules.title: `Core\Http\Client` has no spelling for "wait forever": every bound is a `Duration`, an omitted one inherits `[http.client]`, and expiry throws `TimeoutError`
rules.divergesFromPhp: curl defaults to no timeout and `file_get_contents` to `default_socket_timeout`'s sixty seconds; here there is no `null`, no `0` and no option that means unbounded, so a long call names its own `deadline`

rules.title: An outbound request carries at most one body, named by which of four flat keys it is written under, and a second key or a body on `get` is a compile-time diagnostic
rules.divergesFromPhp: curl takes `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS` as a string, an array or a file handle and infers the encoding from which one it got; here the key names what is sent, two keys are refused before the program runs, and a `Part::file` streams from disk rather than being held whole

rules.title: One `deadline` covers the whole call: the connection, every redirect hop, every retry attempt and every backoff between them
rules.divergesFromPhp: curl's `CURLOPT_TIMEOUT` bounds one transfer, so three attempts at five seconds is a fifteen-second call; here the stated number is the bound on everything

rules.title: `deadline` ends at the head of a streamed reply, its body runs under `idle` and `maxDuration`, and the body is read one way, once
rules.divergesFromPhp: a PHP stream has `default_socket_timeout` and nothing that bounds how long a body may take; here a streamed body has two finite bounds it cannot be without, and reading it twice throws

rules.title: Retry is opt-in, exponential with full jitter that cannot be turned off, and retries only a connection failure, a timeout, `429`, `502`, `503` and `504`
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP's clients have no retry, so every application writes its own loop; here it is three flat options, the jitter is not configurable, and a `Retry-After` header replaces the computed wait

rules.title: A `POST` or `PATCH` is not retried without `retryIdempotencyKey`, and at an ordinary call site the missing key is a compile-time diagnostic
rules.divergesFromPhp: a retried `POST` in PHP does whatever the loop the developer wrote does, including charging a card twice; here the missing key is a red squiggle before the program runs

rules.title: `Core\Http::allowUrl` resolves, checks and pins: it answers a `Target` carrying the URL and every approved address, and the connection is made to one of them
rules.divergesFromPhp: `file_get_contents($userUrl)` and `curl_setopt(CURLOPT_URL, $userUrl)` are a compile-time diagnostic, and the laundered value is a `Target` the program cannot read an address back out of, not a string

rules.title: Every address a name resolves to is checked, one denied refuses the host, and the call falls back across the approved set without ever resolving twice
rules.divergesFromPhp: curl tries every address a name answers and checks none of them; here each is checked before any is tried, one denied refuses the whole host, and the lookup runs off the core

rules.title: `connectTo` names an outbound call's address only where `net.connect_to` names the host, and the address policy and the certificate's host check still apply
rules.divergesFromPhp: `CURLOPT_RESOLVE` takes any host-to-address mapping a script writes; here the host must be granted, the address is judged by the same policy a resolved one is, and the certificate is still checked against the URL's host

rules.title: Redirects are not followed by default; when enabled every hop is re-checked and re-pinned, a denied hop fails the request, and a retry never re-resolves
rules.divergesFromPhp: curl's `FOLLOWLOCATION` is off by default too, but a hop it follows is never checked against anything; here each hop passes the same policy the first URL did and a denied one fails the call rather than being dropped from the chain

rules.title: A redirect from `https` to `http` needs `net.downgrade` for its host and `redirectToHttp` at the call; a plain `http` URL asked for directly stays allowed
rules.divergesFromPhp: curl follows a hop from `https` to `http` silently, so one `Location` header strips a call's TLS; here it needs a grant and a call-site option, and the refusal names the grant

rules.title: A redirect hop to another origin carries none of the caller's own headers, the three named credentials and every `secret` value among them
rules.divergesFromPhp: an `Authorization` header set in a stream context is re-sent to whatever host a `Location` names; here a hop to another origin carries no header the program wrote, that one and every `secret` value included

rules.title: An outbound connection is pooled per core under a key carrying everything the check approved, and returns to the pool only after a reply read to the end under known framing
rules.divergesFromPhp: curl reuses a connection keyed on host and port inside one handle, and PHP's stream functions reuse nothing; here the key carries the pinned address, the client identity and the call's TLS policy, so reuse cannot widen what a check approved

rules.title: `[http.client.proxy]` is the only way an outbound call is proxied: `System` class, written by the operator, and never a call option or an environment variable
rules.divergesFromPhp: curl and PHP's stream wrappers take a proxy from `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` in the environment, or per handle from `CURLOPT_PROXY`; here it is one root-owned block, no environment variable is read, and no program-side spelling exists

rules.title: `resolve` is mandatory: `local` tunnels to the address Novis approved and keeps the pin, `proxy` narrows the policy to the URL's text and warns at every boot
rules.divergesFromPhp: curl hands the proxy the destination's host name in every case, having no approved address to hand it; here that is one of two written answers, the other tunnels to the address the check approved, and the one that gives up the pin is announced at every boot

rules.title: `[http.client.tls]` is the operator's alone: the bundled roots unless files are named, TLS 1.2 unless the floor is raised, and no key log in `production`
rules.divergesFromPhp: `curl.cainfo` and `openssl.cafile` are `ini` settings a script can widen with `ini_set`; here the three keys are `System` class and no code-side spelling for any of them exists

rules.title: `Response::tls()` reports the session a reply arrived over — version, cipher, whether the peer was verified, and its chain — and is `null` when there was none
rules.divergesFromPhp: `curl_getinfo` answers a flat array of thirty-odd keys mixing timings, sizes and TLS facts; here the session is an object read through members and the timings are the trace's

rules.title: Nothing a request can send terminates or wedges a worker: its blast radius is bounded at four named tiers, and the residue is one stated fault class
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no worker process per request to die and be respawned; a request is contained in-process and the process boundary is reserved for one named residue

rules.title: A worker task's root is wrapped in `catch_unwind`: a panic beneath a request fails that request, and one outside any request retires the worker
Every engine-side recursive descent over request data carries a depth counter and refuses past it, with a limit per decoder and `512` for JSON
A helper whose runtime scales with its input polls the request's deadline flag through a bounded-loop combinator, or bounds its input instead
rules.divergesFromPhp: `max_execution_time` fires between statements; here a deadline also reaches inside one `Core` call over a large value, and reaches it by a flag rather than a clock

rules.title: No path reaches `abort()`: nothing on a teardown path panics, teardown is iterative, and an allocation sized by request data is fallible
A core is never blocked on a syscall: filesystem calls, name resolution and waiting on a child go to a blocking pool bounded at twice the core count
A watchdog reads the in-flight deadline each worker already keeps, and reports a core whose oldest deadline is past by a margin
A reported core stops accepting and `max_in_flight` counts its share as unavailable; a wedged worker is never killed in-process
A client that goes away cancels its request tree at the next safepoint; nothing is waited out
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP-FPM learns of a closed tab at the script's next write and holds the worker until `max_execution_time`; here the connection's drop is an event, the tree is cancelled and no worker was ever held

rules.title: Every timeout, deadline and backoff in the engine is computed on a monotonic clock
The floor cannot fill the disk it writes to: a file target rotates under a retention bound, repeats coalesce into one record with a count, and a cache write failure compiles in memory
A page holding generated code is writable while written and executable only after being made read-only
A memory-safety fault in `unsafe` code or a miscompile is the one residue: the process dies, the supervisor restarts it, and the answer is frequency, not a boundary
rules.divergesFromPhp: there is no per-request worker process to absorb an engine crash; a fault of this class loses every request in flight and is answered by a restart in about a cold start
